title: MZ Is it worth moving to RPG Maker MZ or MV after using VX Ace for a while if I own all of them?

posts.author: PuppetWraith
posts.body:
For a while I've been using RPG Maker VX Ace because I started by making mods for games based on Lisa the Painful which was obviously made in Vx Ace. But I kinda wanna "upgrade" in a sense? I've bought MV and MZ for modding other games, and I've heard they run better than VX Ace since it's newer software, but I admit I'm not too knowledgeable on how they run under the hood.
I thought about switching to MZ but I have some conflicting thoughts. First of all, I've heard MV has more and better plugins, but those suggestions might be outdated because it's not like MZ is super new, it's 5 years old.
Also this is much more nitpick-y but I really hate the basic menu for mz. I like the layout more for MV, and I really don't like the mobile UI for MZ... idk I guess if anyone knows any way to change that, it would be cool.
So uh yeah I guess what I'm curious about...
1. Is do MV and MZ run better than VX Ace?
2. Are the plugins for MZ good?
3. Is there any way to change the menu for MZ to look like MV?
Thank you for any help I may get I'm sorry if this is breaking any rules, I really love this engine and community and know people here are super kind.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Personally I prefer using both MV and MZ in tandem. I make my games in MV to take advantage of the vast free (and basically free yanfly plugins) and I prefer the way action sequencing works on it compared to MZ, but I use MZ to make my maps to take advantage of the manual layer control. (You can slap a rmmz project file into your mv game folder and it'll open just fine.)
I'm sure there is a way to make MZ's menu look like MV, but I'm not aware of any existing plugins doing that already.
In any case, I would say upgrade for sure, especially since you already own them!

posts.author: JamesRyan
posts.body: MV is a significant upgrade from VX Ace. You will not regret getting MV or MZ after using VX Ace. I have 2000+ hours on MV after retiring from VX Ace, and I have never regretted.

posts.author: Willibab
posts.body:
Just my experience.
1: I used MV for about 4000 hours and I noticed a immediately how much better MZ ran (I was very reluctant to change)
2/3: MV has SO many good plugins but the FOSSIL project made a ton of them useable in MZ which helped, since there have been so many great plugins for MZ that it's ridiculous
A lot of the more advanced ones are paid but well worth it imo. I agree with you about the HUD/UI. I would strongly suggest checking out
@Aerosys
itch page for a very simple solution that is easy to use.
Im sure there are plenty of free ones too, just with less freedom and options.

posts.author: TRIDIUM
posts.body:
As a VX Ace fanboy, who also hates the default MZ menu, I suggest you switch.
The biggest issue is QoL features and performance. The window is too small in windowed mode, and if you do fullscreen, it does that weird thing where your screen's resolution goes down. There's a single way to get rebindable keys, and it's a bit weird and requires installing a new DLL.
As much as I wany Ace to be a viable option in the big 26, it's not really.
I mainly use MZ over MV for pretty arbitrary reasons, but I'd definitely listen to SG's advice about using them both.
Also, seconding Willibab's recommendation of Aerosys' plguins, they're incredibly easy to use and I've had great results.

Yes. Especially MZ.
PuppetWraith said:
First of all, I've heard MV has more and better plugins, but those suggestions might be outdated because it's not like MZ is super new, it's 5 years old.
Click to expand...
Yes, that's outdated in my opinion. There are already plugins out there that are exclusive to MZ. And let's break it down: What kind of plugins do you need in a regular JRPG? Some menu customizing, visual effects, weather effects, gameplay related stuff such as a questlog, alchemy, crafting, summoning, ... I bet that you find an MZ plugin for every common use-case, even for free.
Furthermore, plugins are muuuuch easier to use in MZ than in all other engines, thanks to plugin commands. These are dropdowns that every plugin provides, where you can simply pick plugin actions (e.g., weather plugin -> change weather -> rain) from a list. That's a true lifesaver.
Additionally, MV & MZ make it super easy to make a browser game that other people can just play without downloading it first.
